cases.purpose: policy-parse accepts the sudoers subset (Defaults, aliases, runas user:group, NOPASSWD, command lists), normalizes insignificant whitespace and comments to identical records and digest, changes the digest for a semantic change, rejects malformed lines with their line number and no partial output, fails closed on @include/#include directives, does not refuse a command path merely containing 'include', and never silently drops a #uid rule.
cases.oracle: sudoers(5) grammar: whitespace around '=', ',', ':' and inside '( )' is insignificant; '#' starts a comment except '#include'/'#includedir' (include directives) and '#uid' user IDs; '@include'/'@includedir' are include directives; commands must be fully qualified paths; Runas is '(user:group)'; timestamp_timeout is numeric. auth's documented contract ('validate and normalize sudoers subset', includes unsupported). Self-consistency: the summary digest is the SHA-256 of the printed normalized records, checked with /usr/bin/sha256sum.
cases.comparison: Exact status and stdout classification lines; diagnostics matched only for the subcommand line-number key.

cases.script:
[[ $(type -t auth) == builtin ]] || { printf 'candidate auth builtin missing\n'; exit 99; }
LC_ALL=C
pp() { auth policy-parse "$1" > out 2> err; rc=$?; }
pp valid.policy; printf 'valid rc=%d\n' "$rc"; /usr/bin/cp out valid.out
last=$(/usr/bin/tail -n 1 valid.out); body=$(/usr/bin/head -n -1 valid.out | /usr/bin/sha256sum)
[[ $last =~ ^summary\ records=([0-9]+)\ digest_sha256=([0-9a-f]{64})$ ]] && printf 'summary=well-formed\n' || printf 'summary=malformed\n'
[[ ${BASH_REMATCH[2]-} == "${body%% *}" ]] && printf 'digest=consistent\n' || printf 'digest=inconsistent\n'
[[ ${BASH_REMATCH[1]-} == $(( $(/usr/bin/wc -l < valid.out) - 1 )) ]] && printf 'records=consistent\n' || printf 'records=inconsistent\n'
[[ -s err ]] && printf 'valid-diag=yes\n' || printf 'valid-diag=no\n'
for v in reformatted spaced; do
  pp "$v.policy"; /usr/bin/cmp -s out valid.out && s=same || s=differ
  printf '%s rc=%d normalized=%s\n' "$v" "$rc" "$s"
done
pp nopasswd.policy; [[ $(/usr/bin/tail -n 1 out) != "$last" ]] && s=differ || s=same
printf 'nopasswd rc=%d digest=%s\n' "$rc" "$s"
for f in bad-*.policy; do
  pp "$f"; e=$(< err) l=-
  [[ $e =~ policy-parse:([0-9]+): ]] && l=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
  [[ -s out ]] && o=nonempty || o=empty
  n=${f#bad-}; printf 'reject %s rc=%d line=%s stdout=%s\n' "${n%.policy}" "$rc" "$l" "$o"
done
pp substring.policy; printf 'substring rc=%d rules=%d\n' "$rc" "$(/usr/bin/grep -c '^rule ' out)"
pp uidform.policy
if (( rc == 0 )) && ! /usr/bin/grep -q '^rule ' out; then printf 'uid-form=silently-dropped\n'; else printf 'uid-form=not-dropped\n'; fi
auth policy-parse > /dev/null 2>&1; printf 'no-arg rc=%d\n' "$?"
auth policy-parse valid.policy valid.policy > /dev/null 2>&1; printf 'two-args rc=%d\n' "$?"
auth policy-parse absent.policy > out 2> err; printf 'absent rc=%d stdout=%s diag=%s\n' "$?" "$([[ -s out ]] && echo nonempty || echo empty)" "$([[ -s err ]] && echo yes || echo no)"
/usr/bin/rm -f out err valid.out
cases.stdout:
valid rc=0
summary=well-formed
digest=consistent
records=consistent
valid-diag=no
reformatted rc=0 normalized=same
spaced rc=0 normalized=same
nopasswd rc=0 digest=differ
reject at-include rc=1 line=3 stdout=empty
reject at-includedir rc=1 line=3 stdout=empty
reject bad-timeout rc=1 line=3 stdout=empty
reject bare-defaults rc=1 line=3 stdout=empty
reject empty-commands rc=1 line=3 stdout=empty
reject hash-include rc=1 line=3 stdout=empty
reject hash-includedir rc=1 line=3 stdout=empty
reject missing-eq rc=1 line=3 stdout=empty
reject relative-command rc=1 line=3 stdout=empty
reject three-word-left rc=1 line=3 stdout=empty
reject unterminated-runas rc=1 line=3 stdout=empty
substring rc=0 rules=1
uid-form=not-dropped
no-arg rc=2
two-args rc=2
absent rc=1 stdout=empty diag=yes

cases.purpose: policy-list renders only rules that apply to the caller (direct name, User_Alias membership, ALL) in file order, expands Cmnd_Alias per entry in --long mode, carries NOPASSWD per entry, binds the projection to the same digest policy-parse reports, reads FILE or an inherited FD identically, refuses another user's projection to a non-root caller, renders empty and no-match policies as an empty projection, and prints nothing for an invalid policy.
cases.oracle: sudoers(5) user matching (user name, User_Alias, ALL, %group via the group database; a nonexistent group matches nobody), sudo(8) -l semantics (lists the invoking user's entries; -U other user needs privilege; listing order follows the policy), and auth's documented 'list caller-filtered sudoers projection' with policy-parse's digest. The VM's uid 2000 account is parity.
cases.comparison: Exact status and projection lines extracted by an in-script awk; the record key names are auth's documented output keys.

files.list.policy:
User_Alias OPS = parity,carol
Cmnd_Alias VIEW = /usr/bin/id,/usr/bin/uptime
parity ALL = (root) /usr/bin/true
OPS ALL = (root) NOPASSWD: VIEW
ALL ALL = (root) /usr/bin/date
bob ALL = (root) /usr/bin/false
%bashosnosuchgrp ALL = (root) /usr/bin/env

cases.script:
[[ $(type -t auth) == builtin ]] || { printf 'candidate auth builtin missing\n'; exit 99; }
printf 'caller=%s\n' "$(/usr/bin/id -un)"
auth policy-list list.policy > short 2> err; printf 'short rc=%d list-lines=%d diag=%s\n' "$?" "$(/usr/bin/grep -c '^list ' short)" "$([[ -s err ]] && echo yes || echo no)"
[[ $(/usr/bin/tail -n 1 short) =~ ^summary\ entries=([0-9]+)\ digest_sha256=([0-9a-f]{64})$ ]] && printf 'short-entries=%s\n' "${BASH_REMATCH[1]}" || printf 'short-summary=malformed\n'
ld=${BASH_REMATCH[2]-}
auth policy-parse list.policy > parsed 2> /dev/null
[[ $(/usr/bin/tail -n 1 parsed) == *"digest_sha256=$ld" && -n $ld ]] && printf 'digest=bound\n' || printf 'digest=unbound\n'
auth policy-list list.policy --long > long 2> /dev/null; printf 'long rc=%d\n' "$?"
/usr/bin/awk '$1 == "entry" { c = ""; n = ""; for (i = 2; i <= NF; i++) { if ($i ~ /^cmd=/) c = substr($i, 5); if ($i ~ /^nopasswd=/) n = substr($i, 10) } print "entry " c " nopasswd=" n }' long
[[ $(/usr/bin/tail -n 1 long) =~ ^summary\ entries=([0-9]+) ]] && printf 'long-entries=%s\n' "${BASH_REMATCH[1]}" || printf 'long-summary=malformed\n'
/usr/bin/grep -Eq '/usr/bin/(false|env)' short long && printf 'foreign=listed\n' || printf 'foreign=absent\n'
auth policy-list list.policy --user "$(/usr/bin/id -un)" > self; /usr/bin/cmp -s self short && printf 'self-user=same\n' || printf 'self-user=differ\n'
auth policy-list 3 3< list.policy > viafd; /usr/bin/cmp -s viafd short && printf 'fd=same\n' || printf 'fd=differ\n'
auth policy-list list.policy --user carol > other 2> err; printf 'other-user rc=%d stdout=%s diag=%s\n' "$?" "$([[ -s other ]] && echo nonempty || echo empty)" "$([[ -s err ]] && echo yes || echo no)"
for p in empty nomatch; do
  auth policy-list "$p.policy" > out 2> /dev/null; rc=$?
  printf '%s rc=%d lines=%d last=%s\n' "$p" "$rc" "$(/usr/bin/wc -l < out)" "$(/usr/bin/tail -n 1 out | /usr/bin/cut -d' ' -f1,2)"
done
auth policy-list invalid.policy > out 2> /dev/null; printf 'invalid rc=%d stdout=%s\n' "$?" "$([[ -s out ]] && echo nonempty || echo empty)"
auth policy-list list.policy --user > /dev/null 2>&1; printf 'user-missing rc=%d\n' "$?"
auth policy-list > /dev/null 2>&1; printf 'no-path rc=%d\n' "$?"
auth policy-list list.policy list.policy > /dev/null 2>&1; printf 'two-paths rc=%d\n' "$?"
/usr/bin/rm -f short long parsed self viafd other out err

cases.purpose: Command-path glob matching follows pathname rules: '*', '?' and bracket expressions never match '/', '!' negates a bracket, a leading ']' and a trailing '-' are literal in a bracket, backslash quotes, and the whole path must match.
cases.oracle: sudoers(5): wildcards in a command path do not match '/' (sudo matches with fnmatch(3) FNM_PATHNAME); POSIX fnmatch bracket rules. Each vector is also computed in the guest by glibc fnmatch(pattern, path, FNM_PATHNAME) through /usr/bin/python3 ctypes, printed as ref.
cases.comparison: Exact candidate stdout, status (0 match, 1 no match, 2 usage) and the glibc reference value per vector.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t auth) == builtin ]] || { printf 'candidate auth builtin missing\n'; exit 99; }
ref() { /usr/bin/python3 -I -c 'import ctypes, sys
libc = ctypes.CDLL("libc.so.6")
print(1 if libc.fnmatch(sys.argv[1].encode(), sys.argv[2].encode(), 1) == 0 else 0)' "$1" "$2"; }
v() { local c; c=$(auth policy-fnmatch "$1" "$2" 2> /dev/null); local rc=$?
  printf '%s %s cand=[%s] rc=%d ref=%s\n' "$1" "$2" "$c" "$rc" "$(ref "$1" "$2")"; }
v '/usr/bin/*' '/usr/bin/id'
v '/usr/bin/*' '/usr/bin/sub/id'
v '/usr/*/id' '/usr/bin/id'
v '/usr/bin/*d' '/usr/bin/id'
v '*' '/usr/bin/id'
v '/usr/bin/?d' '/usr/bin/id'
v '/usr?bin' '/usr/bin'
v '/usr[/]bin' '/usr/bin'
v '/usr/bin/[a-c]at' '/usr/bin/cat'
v '/usr/bin/[a-c]at' '/usr/bin/dat'
v '/usr/bin/[!a-c]at' '/usr/bin/dat'
v '/usr/bin/[!a-c]at' '/usr/bin/cat'
v '/usr/bin/[]]x' '/usr/bin/]x'
v '/usr/bin/[a-]x' '/usr/bin/-x'
v '/usr/bin/\*' '/usr/bin/*'
v '/usr/bin/\*' '/usr/bin/x'
v '/usr/bin/id' '/usr/bin/idx'
v '/usr/bin/id' '/usr/bin/id'
auth policy-fnmatch '/usr/bin/*' > /dev/null 2>&1; printf 'one-arg rc=%d\n' "$?"
auth policy-fnmatch a b c > /dev/null 2>&1; printf 'three-args rc=%d\n' "$?"

cases.purpose: With no /dev/bashos-auth in the guest kernel, probe, privcmd-probe and open fail with a diagnostic naming the device, print nothing, bind no FDVAR and leak no descriptor; usage errors stay status 2. This is the absent-device obligation only; the VERSION ioctl, fd counters and slot cleanup remain a genuine capability gap.
cases.oracle: auth's documented contract (probe prints abi=MAJOR.MINOR features=0xHEX from the device; open binds the device fd into FDVAR) and fail-closed behaviour: open(2) of a missing path fails with ENOENT, so nothing may be printed or bound. Status 2 for usage errors, 1 for operational failure.
cases.comparison: Exact status, stdout presence, FDVAR binding and descriptor count of the shell process before and after.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t auth) == builtin ]] || { printf 'candidate auth builtin missing\n'; exit 99; }
[[ -e /dev/bashos-auth ]] && printf 'device=present\n' || printf 'device=absent\n'
nfd() { nopen=0; local i; for ((i = 3; i < 64; i++)); do { : >&"$i"; } 2> /dev/null && ((nopen++)); done; }
nfd; before=$nopen
auth probe > out 2> err; printf 'probe rc=%d stdout=%s diag-names-device=%s\n' "$?" "$([[ -s out ]] && echo nonempty || echo empty)" "$([[ $(< err) == *"/dev/bashos-auth"* ]] && echo yes || echo no)"
auth privcmd-probe > out 2> err; printf 'privcmd-probe rc=%d stdout=%s diag=%s\n' "$?" "$([[ -s out ]] && echo nonempty || echo empty)" "$([[ -s err ]] && echo yes || echo no)"
auth privcmd-probe extra > /dev/null 2>&1; printf 'privcmd-probe-extra rc=%d\n' "$?"
unset authfd; auth open authfd 2> err; printf 'open rc=%d bound=%s diag=%s\n' "$?" "${authfd+yes}" "$([[ -s err ]] && echo yes || echo no)"
auth open > /dev/null 2>&1; printf 'open-no-var rc=%d\n' "$?"
nfd; [[ $before == "$nopen" ]] && printf 'fds=unchanged\n' || printf 'fds=changed\n'
auth > /dev/null 2>&1; printf 'no-subcommand rc=%d\n' "$?"
auth bogus > /dev/null 2> err; printf 'unknown rc=%d diag=%s\n' "$?" "$([[ -s err ]] && echo yes || echo no)"
auth --help > out 2> /dev/null; printf 'help rc=%d first=[%s]\n' "$?" "$(/usr/bin/head -n 1 out)"
/usr/bin/rm -f out err
cases.stdout:
device=absent
probe rc=1 stdout=empty diag-names-device=yes
privcmd-probe rc=1 stdout=empty diag=yes
privcmd-probe-extra rc=2
open rc=1 bound= diag=yes
open-no-var rc=2
fds=unchanged
no-subcommand rc=2
unknown rc=2 diag=yes
help rc=0 first=[Talk to /dev/bashos-auth - kernel-mediated authority tokens.]
